human-prose.what: the site's own sentences in plain wording, after Wikipedia:Signs of AI writing (lib/humanprose.js): no spaced em dashes in prose, no canned fit lines ('Standard length — a normal evening's watch'), no rhetorical snippet hook ('— but is it worth your evening?'), one plain critics' summary per shape instead of rotating flourishes, plain hub/list intros and footer. near-copy-085.what: near-copy editions hidden from Google at 0.85 similarity instead of 0.90, by film (lib/googlehide.js nearCopyThreshold). At 0.90 the rule hides 129 editions today, and 2,001 visible pairs sit at 0.80 to 0.90. At 0.85 it hides 552 editions of 180 films (India never; the edition with the most clicks stays), 423 more than today, and their sister pages lose them from hreflang. Two stages so no build changes more than about 700 pages: 50% at the 6 Nov afternoon build (390 hidden, after the score-link build), 100% on 7 Nov (552). Owner's call, 5 Nov 2026.

No studio or platform can pay for a score.') removed; its 'How the score works' link moves to the end of the card's Audience/Critics line (lib/filmpage.js fcScoreSection, scoreLink). Every film page including hidden ones, by slug. 10% at the 5 Nov 12:16 UTC build; switched to 100% at once for the next build at the owner's request (5 Nov 2026). arrival-alerts.what: arrival alerts (lib/alerts.js, js/app.js, sw.js): after saving a film that isn't streaming yet, the homepage offers one web-push ping for when it starts streaming in that edition; a switch under My List turns it on or off. The build sends after the deploy and the live check, from the manifest's verified live state, at most one alert per reader a day, never the same film twice. A site-wide switch, not per film: any percent above 0 is on, 0 removes the offer at the next build and stops sending. Needs VAPID_PUBLIC_KEY (variable) and VAPID_PRIVATE_KEY (secret); without them nothing is offered. Mock-up 5 Nov; every edition at once at the owner's request.

page-v3.what: film page v3 (owner's sequence, 28 Oct 2026): backdrop, title with status tag, meta line, audience + platform pills, score card with one Audience/Critics line, full Story, director, cast, Good to know (with the where-to-watch row), episodes, trailer, franchise, similar, FAQ. No answer card, CTA, prose fillers, fit rows or separate Where to watch block. Mock-up first. Switched to 100% at once on 28 Oct 2026 at the owner's request after the mock-up.

arrival-record.what: the arrival record on film pages (lib/dated.js useSightings, lib/windows.js arrivalHtml): 'Reached Prime Video 29 days after cinemas. We spotted it there on Saturday 7 Nov, overnight.' Live sightings only (written within a day of the first date; not the archive's first day; not a title out two years before), the part of the day and never a time, the days counted to the day shown; the Good to know 'OTT arrival' row goes where the line says the same. Approved by the owner after the 9 Nov mock-ups; 10/25/50/100% on 10–13 Nov.
